doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Being one of the guys, not a diva, and not missing touring
summary: She rejects the label diva, calls herself a musician, and says she missed nothing by staying home.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No, because I never really . . . I wasn‘t about being anything more than just . . . I‘ve always been one of the guys. I‘m a musician, you see. I‘m not . . . I kind of resent the fact you‘re a . . . when they call you . . . what is the thing they call you, what is it?
I do not like that at all. I‘m not a diva. I‘m a musician, you know, and as I say, I like to hang in with the guys and play. But a diva? I‘m no diva. Shit, I‘m not a diva. I‘m a musician.
But even as a musician, this is your first recording that could lead to other gigs. How did you . . . well, you were already gigging every day, so I guess you . . .
Yeah, I came home and I was doing, you know, every night playing the gigs.
So you didn‘t feel like you were missing anything by not touring?
No, no, no, uh-uh. No, no, no. I didn‘t.
Or not having a recording on the [unclear]?
No, no. I didn‘t miss anything. I was one of the guys. It was my pleasure to sit down and hang out with the guys. They would play all night long, you know, because that was my thing.
